summary: Clallam County, WA Army Aircraft Warning Service post 'Bald' with a 1942 cabin; not occupied in 1943; turned to the Coast Guard; gone, with erosion reported at the cabin site.

facts.design: Cabin of native materials, built 1942 (two stoves, per the AWS record)
facts.status_note: Cabin gone. A WillhiteWeb account recalls a cable handrail and steps in the early 1980s and, undated, says erosion has collapsed much of the cabin site.
facts.agency: Army Aircraft Warning Service, later U.S. Coast Guard (per the AWS record)

events.note: Cabin of native materials built with difficulty (AWS record); listed as a 1942 cabin on firelookout.com.
March 12, 1943 AWS record: station complete but not occupied, no satisfactory radio hookup.
Site turned over to the Coast Guard on October 1, 1943, after the state declined it.
firelookout.com lists the site as abandoned in 1944. The AWS record gives the 1943 transfer instead.

site is in Clallam County, Washington
the Army managed an AWS site called Bald on the beach near Lake Ozette

evidence.supports: not a regular fire lookout; state did not want the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1944 as the year the site was abandoned; the AWS record says it was turned over to the Coast Guard on October 1, 1943. The story gives both dates.

firelookout.com's page lists the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR as the source; the AWS record says the state did not want the site and it went to the Coast Guard. The story follows the AWS record.
firelookout.com gives 300 feet and the willhite page gives 100 feet. The elevation is not used in the story.

sources.title: Bald AWS Observation Post - Ozette Beach

notes_for_editor: Do not merge with us-wa-aws-ozette-lake. That record is a separate AWS station on the east side of Ozette Lake, a 14 x 32 cabin reached only by boat. This record is 'Bald' near the beach, with a 1942 cabin. The main source (WillhiteWeb) is a personal site with undated recollections, so its early-1980s remark is weaker than the AWS dates. The firelookout.com dates and the AWS record disagree (1944 vs 1 October 1943), and the story reports both. Access is not set because no source describes it today. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 4 page reads.
